name: ClashEval
description: ClashEval is a dataset designed to evaluate large language models' ability to discern between their internal prior knowledge and external retrieved evidence, especially when the retrieved content contains errors. It includes over 1200 questions across six domains with perturbed retrieved content to test model susceptibility to adopting incorrect information.
reputation: A newer benchmark that has attracted interest for testing retrieval robustness and conflict between parametric knowledge and retrieved evidence, but it is not yet as established as long-running QA benchmarks.
notes: Focuses on LLMs' ability to reject incorrect retrieved content and adopt correct information, highlighting challenges in retrieval-augmented generation.
